fs/glob#

MatchingPaths snapshots every path below root that matches a relative glob pattern.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let sources is @Path = MatchingPaths(
    root: project,
    pattern: "src/*.ok",
).map() -> path { path; };

Description#

MatchingPaths snapshots every path below root that matches a relative glob pattern. Results are globally lexicographically sorted before cursor() returns. Patterns always use / between segments, including on Windows.

Files immediately inside src:

Recursive test discovery:

for MatchingPaths(root: project, pattern: "**/*-test.ok") -> path {
    output.writeln(path.string());
}

* matches zero or more Unicode characters inside one segment, ? matches exactly one, and classes accept literals, ranges and leading ! negation:

MatchingPaths(root: logs, pattern: "202[4-6]-[!0]?-*.log");

Matching is case-sensitive on every platform and includes leading dots. ** is recursive only as a complete segment and matches zero or more path segments. A matching symlink path is returned, but traversal never enters it.

Public API#

object MatchingPaths#

object MatchingPaths does Iterating<Path>

Every path below root that matches a glob pattern, sorted: * and ? within a name, classes like [a-z] and [!0], and ** as a whole part for any depth.
